extracted.intended_audience: NIH study section reviewers / grant reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for NIH peer reviewers on providing feedback about meeting format and review process quality, especially after virtual study section meetings. Emphasizes using the post‑study‑section survey to communicate issues to NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention span and concentration during virtual meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Report your attention span and concentration during virtual (Zoom) study section meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the post‑study‑section survey to record whether attention and concentration suffered in the virtual format. The page lists this explicitly as a survey question to answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer engagement levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and report how engaged reviewers were during the meeting (e.g., degree of participation, attentiveness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond honestly on the post‑study‑section survey about reviewer engagement; the author frames this as a key data point NIH needs to understand the consequences of virtual meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity of panel discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the productivity and quality of panel discussions (how useful, thorough, and decision‑oriented they were).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate on the survey whether panel discussions were productive in the virtual format compared with in‑person, since this is central to the argument that virtual meetings have been a 'total disaster.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferences between in‑person and Zoom formats
rubrics_metrics.description: State your format preference (in‑person vs. Zoom) and why, including comparisons of effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly communicate format preference on the survey; the post urges reviewers to tell NIH that not having in‑person meetings has been a major problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give honest infrastructure feedback to the funding agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide candid feedback about the review infrastructure (meeting format, logistics, technology) rather than limiting comments to proposal scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author encodes a normative duty: 'A "good reviewer" duty includes giving honest infrastructure feedback to the funding agency, not just scoring proposals.' Use the post‑study‑section survey as the vehicle for that feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help fix the review system (reviewer responsibility beyond scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that reviewers have a responsibility to help improve the review system itself by reporting systemic problems and suggestions for change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that the reviewer's role 'extends to helping fix the review system' and recommends taking the single productive action of communicating to NIH about the harms of lacking in‑person meetings.
